coverage: Complete novella in both English editions: named people, identifiable household and incident roles, and named personal allusions. Central identity revelation released only after Lanyon explicitly identifies Hyde.

entities.name: Gabriel John Utterson
entities.body: The London lawyer whose friends include Dr. Jekyll and Dr. Lanyon.

entities.name: Dr. Henry Jekyll
entities.body: A London doctor and longtime friend of Utterson and Lanyon.

snapshots.body: Utterson’s doctor friend, who transforms into Edward Hyde.

entities.name: Edward Hyde
entities.body: The man Enfield identifies as having trampled a young girl in the street.

snapshots.body: The man named as Jekyll’s beneficiary in his will, whose background troubles Utterson.
The identity and altered physical form assumed by Henry Jekyll.

entities.name: Richard Enfield
entities.body: Utterson’s distant relative and companion on his Sunday walks.

entities.name: Dr. Hastie Lanyon
entities.body: A London doctor and old friend of Utterson and Jekyll.

entities.name: Poole
entities.body: Dr. Jekyll’s butler.

entities.name: Sir Danvers Carew
entities.body: An elderly Member of Parliament and a client of Utterson.

entities.name: Mr. Guest
entities.body: Utterson’s head clerk, skilled at examining handwriting.

entities.name: Inspector Newcomen
entities.body: The Scotland Yard inspector working with Utterson on the Carew case.

entities.name: Bradshaw
entities.body: A footman in Dr. Jekyll’s household.

entities.name: Dr. Denman
entities.body: The surgeon who previously owned the premises now used by Jekyll.

entities.name: The girl in Enfield’s account
entities.body: The young girl in Enfield’s account of his late-night walk.

entities.name: The doctor in Enfield’s account
entities.body: The doctor with an Edinburgh accent who attends the injured girl.

entities.name: The girl’s father
entities.body: The father of the injured girl in Enfield’s account.

entities.name: Lanyon’s butler
entities.body: The servant who admits Utterson to Dr. Lanyon’s house.

entities.name: The maid at the window
entities.body: The young maid watching the street from an upstairs window.

entities.name: Hyde’s housekeeper
entities.body: The woman who keeps Hyde’s rooms in Soho.

entities.name: Jekyll’s housemaid
entities.body: The maid among the frightened servants in Dr. Jekyll’s house.

entities.name: Jekyll’s cook
entities.body: The cook in Dr. Jekyll’s household.

entities.name: The knife-boy
entities.body: The young servant in Jekyll’s household whose duties include cleaning cutlery.

entities.name: The locksmith
entities.body: The tradesman called to open the locked door to Jekyll’s cabinet.

entities.name: The carpenter
entities.body: The tradesman assisting with the locked door to Jekyll’s cabinet.

entities.name: Cain
entities.body: The biblical brother of Abel, invoked in Utterson’s remark about leaving others to their own choices.

entities.name: Satan
entities.body: The devil of Christian tradition, used in comparisons with Hyde.

entities.name: Damon
entities.body: One of a legendary pair of devoted friends, alongside Pythias.

entities.name: Pythias
entities.body: One of a legendary pair of devoted friends, alongside Damon.

entities.name: Dr. Fell
entities.body: The figure in a familiar rhyme about disliking someone without knowing why.
